svg.title: A thread reaches any DRAM
svg.text: one call, and Tensix cores bring the range to the thread
D0 to D7 are the eight DRAM banks. The range (outlined) lies in D0; work cluster 1's region (dashed) in D6, its own bank.

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: the thread empties its cluster's cache
kmx_evict, 21 µs: from 160 KiB; a sweep below
for cores 0 to 3; sent again if it is busy
the cores copy, bank to bank
16 KiB chunks; four cores reach the bank's rate
from: a range of any bank, or a tensor's pages.
kmx_store is the same the other way: the dirty
lines written back, then the cores copy them out.
A cluster's own cache reaches one bank only;
its loads through a NoC window move 0.024 GB/s.
3 copy: 64 MiB in 1.06 ms, 63.4 GB/s on four cores
2 the command; the event comes back the same way

svg.text: kmx_fetch from another bank of the card
kmx_fetch of a tensor another island holds
kmx_store into a tensor another island holds
the X280's own loads through a NoC window
One card: four Tensix cores, work cluster 1, every byte checked. Another island: two cards, 16 cores, each run of pages one line,
straight between the two DRAMs over four links (59.5 GB/s), every word checked; on one island the same call is the local copy.
the call in time, and what it costs
